thread.title: Yahoo Finance's stock market outlook, October 26

author: Myles Udland
title: Yahoo Finance's stock market outlook, October 26
text:
The wild week for stocks continues.
After markets were battered on Wednesday, all three major indexes staged big rallies on Thursday as many of the losers from the previous day turned into market leaders, with the tech-heavy Nasdaq rising almost 3% and the Russell 2000 gaining more than 2%.
The Dow on Thursday added 401 points, or 1.6%, lead by Microsoft ( MSFT ), which gained almost 6%, while the S&P 500 added 1.8%, or 49 points, and the Nasdaq rose 2.9%, or 209 points.
Stocks on Friday, however, will be dealing with the fallout from a noisy and negative block of after-hours earnings reports that saw both Amazon ( AMZN ) and Alphabet ( GOOGL ) fall sharply after reporting disappointing third quarters.
Amazon shares were off as much as 9% in after hours trading on Thursday after the company’s third quarter revenue came in at $56.6 billion, below the Street’s forecast for revenue of $57.1 billion. The company also guided to weaker-than-expected fourth-quarter revenue. Profit for Amazon topped estimates in the third quarter, with the company reporting earnings per share of $5.75 against expectations for EPS of $3.14.
Amazon shares were dropping after hours on Thursday after third quarter results that disappointed Wall Street. Amazon, along with tech peer Alphabet, which also declined in after hours trading, could pressure markets on Friday. (AP Photo/Mark Lennihan, File) More Alphabet shares were also dropping after hours with the search giant reporting revenue of $33.7 billion against Wall Street estimates for revenue of $34 billion. Earnings per share in the third quarter did top estimates for Alphabet, with the company reporting EPS of $13.06 against the Street’s forecast for $10.42 in earnings per share.
Disappointing results from Amazon and Alphabet pressured all of the FAANG names in late trading on Thursday, with Netflix ( NFLX ), Apple ( AAPL ), and Facebook ( FB ) all falling in sympathy.
Investors did get some positive earnings news out of the tech sector on Thursday, however, as shares of Intel ( INTC ) were higher in after hours trade as the chip giant reported better than expected top and bottom-line results.
On Friday morning, investors will also be greeted by the week’s biggest economic data point, which is the first look at third-quarter GDP growth.
Economists expect the report to show the economy grew at an annualized rate of 3.3% during the third three-month block of the year, a slowdown from the 4.2% pace of growth seen in the second quarter but still indicating the economy is growing at a very strong pace. The economic calendar will also bring investors the final look at consumer sentiment in October from the University of Michigan.
And on the earnings front, Moody’s ( MCO ), Philips 66 ( PSX ), Colgate-Palmolive ( CL ), and Weyerhaeuser ( WY ) are among the notable companies set to report results.
—
Myles Udland is a writer at Yahoo Finance. Follow him on Twitter @MylesUdland
